taskDescription: Click ONLY the finding(s) that specifically distinguish vitamin B12 deficiency from folate deficiency. For a multi-word finding, click every word. Do not click findings that are common to both.
textField: A 55-year-old strict vegan has fatigue and *tingling* in both feet. Blood film shows macrocytes and hypersegmented neutrophils, which occur in both B12 and folate deficiency, and homocysteine is raised in both. Serum *MMA* is raised, and only B12 deficiency causes *subacute* *combined* *degeneration* of the spinal cord.

overallFeedback.feedback: Macrocytes, hypersegmented neutrophils and raised homocysteine appear in both folate and B12 deficiency. A raised MMA (methylmalonic acid) and subacute combined degeneration of the cord are specific to B12, because methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (adenosylcobalamin-dependent) is impaired only when B12 is deficient; folate alone cannot correct or prevent this neurological damage.
